subject.title: Agent confabulates completed actions on Telegram surface — same config works reliably on Claude Code/Codex

question: Should OpenClaw add core action-claim verification or fail-closed semantics for Telegram/ACP turns beyond the current private-final warning and message_tool_only delivery contract?
rationale: The observable bug is real and high-impact, but the safe fix depends on privacy, delivery, and model-compliance policy that automation should not choose.

options.title: Define Core Verification Policy
options.body: Specify which claimed side effects must be proven, how missing proof is surfaced, and when private finals may remain private before implementation starts.

options.title: Limit To Narrow Diagnostics
options.body: Keep current delivery behavior and add only operator-visible warnings or live-repro instrumentation for suspected confabulation.

options.title: Fold Into Existing Delivery Issues
options.body: Track only the narrower stranded-final and cron hallucination issues if maintainers decide arbitrary action-claim verification is out of scope.

recommendation.title: Define Core Verification Policy
recommendation.body: Specify which claimed side effects must be proven, how missing proof is surfaced, and when private finals may remain private before implementation starts.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses delivery privacy, user trust, and product policy rather than a single Telegram line-level repair.
